newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil stake for sale is from shares/loans scheme.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil stake for sale is from shares/loans scheme.

text.p: A five percent block of shares in Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil, which is to be auctioned next month, is the government-owned stake mortgaged in December 1995 under the shares-for-loans programme, a LUKoil spokesman said on Monday.
Earlier the Federal Property Fund said it was auctioning the five percent stake, which comprises 35.73 million shares, at a commercial tender on June 20.

Spokesman Dmitry Dolgov said the shares represented the stake put under the management of LUKoil and Bank Imperial 1-1/2 years ago against a loan of $35.001 million to the government, guaranteed by Slavyansky Kommerchesky Bank.
The starting price for the stake is 250 billion roubles ($43 million), he said. Bids will be accepted until June 19 and the results published on June 20.

The Federal Property Fund and LUKoil would split the excess over the original loan, with the fund receiving 70 percent of the difference, and OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil getting 30 percent of the excess, he said.
At recent sales of oil company stakes mortgaged under the shares-for-loans programme, winning bids have been barely above the starting price.
LUKoil ordinaries were trading at about $15 on Monday, putting a value of about $535 million on the stake.
Under the shares-for-loans programme in late 1995, the government transferred control of state-owned stakes in partly privatised companies to investors in return for loans to the government.
Winners had the right to manage the shares and from September last year they could sell them, with the government repaying the loan from the proceeds and both parties splitting the difference.

The scheme raised urgently needed cash for the government without dumping privatised shares on the market, but the rules were changed frequently and many tenders were won by banks or companies close to those organising the sale for the government.
